linkedin.title: Most news feeds are designed to keep you scrolling, not to keep you informed.
linkedin.body:
We spend hours catching up on the world, yet we often feel less informed than when we started. The problem isn't the volume of news. It is the lack of focus. Most algorithms prioritize engagement metrics over your actual interests, showing you whatever is most likely to trigger a reaction rather than what actually matters to your life or career.

Personalization shouldn't mean being trapped in a bubble of opinions you already hold. Real personalization is about relevance. It is about cutting through the noise to find the stories that affect your industry, your community, and your curiosity. It is about reclaiming your time so you can read less and understand more.

We built Headlinne because we believe technology should work for the reader, not the advertiser. A news feed should be a tool for clarity, not a test of your attention span.

beats.caption: Experts warn this approach is actually dangerous nonsense.

story_card.headline: Brain organoids track time over five years
story_card.standfirst: Scientists grew human brain cells in a lab to see how they mature on their own.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Researchers grew human brain organoids for five years to see if they mature on their own.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: The cells were kept in culture to mimic how a natural brain develops over time.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: It proves brain cells follow internal biological programs even outside a human body.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Future studies on how these organoids record time without a full organism present.

story_card.caption:
Scientists have found that human brain organoids can record the passage of time over multiple years in a lab.

This study published in Nature shows that brain cells continue to mature using their own internal biological programs. This development happened entirely outside the context of a living human organism.
